- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in subsequent periods; apply a “lag correction” by reducing forecast by 1–3% in the next 2–3 periods.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% in next period; if below, increase by 1–2%.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% immediately.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model tends to overfit recent trends; apply smoothing filter to dampen momentum bias.
